lines.src: E101 spec #16 ('Coordinate telephone outlet locations w/owner; 3/4" conduit w/pull-string') · A550 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND 'PHONE' · A552 plan 01 tag 905 · E101 symbol legend (18") · A530 GN D (12") · G402 general note 9 · E400 GN #1
lines.instanceNote: The ITEM is HIGH (E101 spec #16 mandates the outlet plus the conduit and pull string; PHONE is on the legend; tag 905 is placed once on A552). The COUNT of 1 is DERIVED from the FF&E tag, not from a printed drop schedule — no sheet states per-room telephone drop counts. HEIGHT OPEN, 12" vs 18". THE NOTE THAT BITES ON AN ACCESSIBLE KEY: G402 general note 9 verbatim — 'PROVIDE AN ELECTRICAL OUTLET WITHIN 48" OF THE TELEPHONE CONNECTION. THE OUTLET MUST HAVE A CLEAR FLOOR SPACE AND MEET ACCESSIBILITY STANDARDS FOR REACH RANGE.'
lines.verifyAtPunch: Plug the handset in and confirm dial tone. Measure the distance from the telephone connection to the nearest electrical outlet and record it against 48" MAX (G402 guestroom-bath general note 9), and confirm that outlet has clear floor space and sits in the accessible reach range — on an accessible key this one is inspectable. Confirm the 3/4" conduit with pull string is there at the box (E101 spec #16). Confirm the plate is offset roughly 6" from the adjacent room's box (E400 GN1, no back-to-back). Measure and record the height.

lines.label: Wireless access point in a 3-GANG BOX MOUNTED VERTICALLY under the desk — keynote 44 verbatim: 'WAP IN 3-GANG BOX MOUNTED VERTICALLY UNDER DESK. MAINTAIN 6" BETWEEN ALL BOXES, TYP ALL GUESTROOMS. COORDINATE WAP LOCATION WITH CASEGOODS TO AVOID CONFLICTS'
lines.where: Under the desk on the working wall; kn44 requires ≥6" between all boxes and coordination with the casegoods.
lines.src: A550 kn44 (verbatim, 'TYP ALL GUESTROOMS') and A550 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND 'WAP (18")' · placed on A550, A551, A555 — NOT in A552 view 04's placed keynote list
lines.instanceNote: DB-ONLY FOR 118. The DB carries the WAP on 118 at HIGH, but A552 view 04's placed keynote list is 3, 10, 14, 15, 16, 24, 25, 28, 45, 46, 47, 49, 50, 51 — kn44 is NOT in it, while A550, A551 and A555 all carry it and kn44's own text says 'TYP ALL GUESTROOMS'. The keynote text and the sheet's placement list disagree. COMPOUNDING (conflict LV-2): NO WAP appears in ANY E-series schedule — no count, no circuit, no cabling design, no power source; Hilton requires an approved integrator per connectedroom.hilton.com, so the punch reference is the integrator's as-built, not the E-series. SETTLES IT: read A552 view 04 at full scale for the WAP symbol under the desk — a two-minute read. Do not assume 118 has one and do not assume it does not.
lines.verifyAtPunch: Look under the desk: is a WAP in a 3-gang box there — yes or no? Record it with a photo either way. If present: box mounted VERTICALLY, at least 6" clear of every adjacent box, not buried or heat-trapped behind the casegoods, powered and with its status LED normal. Then shut the guestroom door and confirm a phone gets internet at the bed and in the bath. If absent, do NOT write it up yet — kn44 is not in A552 view 04's placed list and no E-series schedule carries a WAP at all.

lines.label: Optional wired data connection at the desktop grommet (kn46) — either a CAT6 RJ-45 jack and patch cord, or a patch cord from a WAP port
lines.where: At the desktop grommet on the working-wall desk, directly above the WAP position.
lines.src: A552 view 04 kn46 (placed) · A550 keynote legend line 161 · A550 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND 'OPTIONAL DATA' (a symbol in its own right)
lines.instanceNote: kn46 IS in A552 view 04's placed list and OPTIONAL DATA is its own legend symbol, so something lands at the grommet — 'OPTION' in kn46 describes the two DELIVERY METHODS, not whether to install: A) add a CAT6 RJ-45 jack and patch cord through the grommet, or B) run a patch cord from a WAP port through the grommet. WHICH ONE WAS BOUGHT IS NOT STATED ANYWHERE (packages/electrical.md open item 6 — a x115 cost item: option A is a real jack, option B is near-zero cost). Under either, a guest must get a working wired connection at the desk, so the walker cannot mis-punch it. Do NOT call 'nothing there' a defect until the scope question is answered by the owner/franchise or the low-voltage subcontract. SETTLES IT: the integrator's submittal.
lines.verifyAtPunch: Look into the desktop grommet and record which of the three you find: a CAT6 RJ-45 jack (option A), a patch cord run up from a WAP port (option B), or nothing. Plug a laptop in at the desk and confirm a working wired link — under either option a guest must get one. Do NOT call 'nothing there' a defect; the scope question is unanswered.

lines.label: Connected Room edge controller — the in-room head-end the TV data jack patches into. NO mark, NO symbol, NO schedule entry anywhere in the set.
lines.where: NOT LOCATED ON ANY SHEET. The only clue is kn47's own cable topology — TV CAT6 in smurf tube to the WAP under the desk, then a patch cord to the edge controller — which puts it at or near the WAP. That is inference from the cable path, not a printed location.
lines.src: A552 kn47 (both options end 'PATCH CORD TO EDGE CONTROLLER FOR CONNECTED ROOM') · E101 GN #8 (names 'connected room' among the exposed connections requiring Panduit locks)
lines.instanceNote: DB GAP — no row exists. What the edge controller physically is, where it mounts, who supplies it and whether it is already installed are all UNKNOWN. It is named twice in kn47 and once in E101 GN #8 and appears NOWHERE else — no mark, no symbol on the power & signal legend, no E-series schedule, no count. Consistent with the broader condition: no telecom riser, rack elevation, port count or head-end equipment schedule exists anywhere in this set, so the low-voltage package is effectively owner/vendor-designed. qty 1 is read off kn47's singular 'THE EDGE CONTROLLER'. SETTLES IT: the Hilton-approved integrator's submittal — walk the first room with the integrator and record what and where it is, then punch the rest against that.
lines.verifyAtPunch: Find it and record exactly where it is (behind the TV / under the desk / in the closet / not present) with a photo. Confirm the TV CAT6 patch cord lands on it and that the exposed connection carries a PANDUIT LOCK (E101 GN8). Confirm it is powered. Then test end to end from a guest device — cast to the TV and confirm Connected Room features work. Walk the first room with the integrator and punch the other 114 against what you record here.

lines.label: Doorbell on/off switch (keyed note 28) — 'DOORBELL ON/OFF SWITCH (COMMUNICATION FEATURES ROOMS ONLY) SIGNAGE AS REQ'D.' EXPECT ZERO IN 217.
lines.where: Guest-room entry door (GR-1) in a communication-features key; the on/off switch is an in-room device (kn28 is also carried on the bed-wall elevations of A555/A556).
lines.src: A552 view 04 kn28 (PLACED) · A550 POWER & SIGNAL LEGEND 'DOORBELL (DB)' · A100 Guestroom Matrix and G001 Unit Mix (118 = 'King Studio ACC MOD, CD', separate from every HI row) · coordination_issues C-04 / PH-GU-002
lines.instanceNote: EXPECT ZERO — AND THIS IS A TRAP, because the DB carries a row for it AND kn28 IS in A552 view 04's placed keynote list, so a field electrician reading 118's own sheet sees a DB symbol. The keynote TEXT restricts it: 'DOORBELL ON/OFF SWITCH (COMMUNICATION FEATURES ROOMS ONLY)'. 118 is MOBILITY-accessible, not hearing-accessible — both matrices type it 'King Studio ACC MOD, CD', a row separate from every HI row, and C-04 proves the two attributes are independent (317 mobility-accessible has zero strobes; 309 a plain QQ has three). Building-wide the communication-features register DOES NOT EXIST — 12 required, 8 located, floor 1 never scanned — so NO first-floor room can be punched for a doorbell yet. qty 0 = confirm absent, and check specifically for a doorbell that should not be there.
lines.verifyAtPunch: Check the corridor face of the entry door for a doorbell push and the inside of the room for an on/off switch — confirm NEITHER is present, and that there is no orphan blank plate, capped box or filled hole at either location. If one IS installed, photograph it and log it: kn28 restricts the doorbell to communication-features rooms and 118 is mobility-accessible, not hearing-accessible.
